reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that social progress is driven by the interplay of uncertainty, evolving wants, and knowledge. The first primitive establishes that progress requires resolving uncertainty through competitive markets, where uniform pricing ensures efficient resource use. The second introduces the complexity of human wants—whether accidental, predictable, or engineered—which directly impacts profit generation. Unexpected want changes yield pure profit or loss, while predictable ones do not. Deliberate changes are treated as economic operations, subject to competitive feedback. The third primitive links knowledge and invention to technological advancement, which further reshapes production and consumption. These primitives form a triadic system: uncertainty drives market adjustment, want evolution shapes demand, and knowledge enables supply-side transformation. Each layer interacts dynamically, creating feedback loops that define the trajectory of social progress. Failure modes include overconfidence in predictability, misalignment of incentives, and insufficient adaptive capacity in institutions.
